title: Entity-identity merges must be conservative, evidence-gated, auditable, and reversible
requirement: Where a Clank merges observations or records from multiple sources/sightings into a single canonical entity, the default posture MUST prefer a missed merge over a false merge: insufficient evidence of sameness MUST leave two records unresolved/separate rather than forcing them into one canonical identity. A key or signal used only to surface or propose a candidate match MUST NOT, by itself, be treated as sufficient grounds to commit that match as canonical identity. Any merge that does get committed automatically (without a human decision) MUST be evidence-gated (based on a criterion stronger than the coarse candidate-surfacing signal alone), auditable (the basis for the merge decision is recorded), and reversible or otherwise information-preserving — the pre-merge records and their original per-source identity MUST remain reconstructable, even if the canonical view no longer displays them separately.
trigger: Applies to any Clank that merges records from more than one source, sighting, or observation into a canonical entity representation. A Clank whose canonical records are strictly one-to-one with source observations (no merging occurs at all) is out of scope. Regional variants: a Clank MAY legitimately treat the same base product in different regions as distinct canonical entities, or as one entity with regional facts attached — this standard does not choose between those architectures (see docs/data-ontology/pass0/clusters/regional-variant-identity.md, held as a separate, still-unresolved concern); it binds only the evidence/reversibility discipline of whatever merge decisions a Clank actually makes.
rationale: Evidenced by four independent, dated incidents of the same shape, escalating to severe: oem-radar's coarse model_key fallback merged two genuinely different SKUs sharing a model_key and tier word, and the identical bug class recurred a second time in different code (Evidence Fusion identity-linking) months later; feature-phone-clank's IDENTITY_ANOMALY comparison bug; tablet-clank's Apple Store carrier/unlocked URL deduplication failure produced 48 false new_product events; semiconductor-intelligence's single-shared-entity clustering flaw produced a merged-entity artifact that became the database's highest-scored 'story,' forcing a full architectural rebuild rather than a patch. Against this, watch-clank's conservative, evidence-gated allowlist policy produced zero confirmed false merges in the surveyed evidence. The asymmetry (a missed merge surfaces as a visible, benign duplicate; a false merge silently corrupts canonical state and propagates to every downstream alert/decision) is independently confirmed by every incident in the corpus and is the basis for defaulting to conservatism rather than leaving the tradeoff unscoped.
forbidden: Committing a canonical merge solely on a known-coarse identifier (a candidate-surfacing key) when a stronger discriminator that could resolve the ambiguity is present in the records under consideration (or in the merged record) and conflicts with the merge
Destroying or overwriting per-source identity information as part of canonicalization, such that the original distinct records can no longer be reconstructed after a merge
An automatic merge with no recorded basis for why it was judged safe (untraceable merges)
acceptance: Ambiguous candidates (insufficient evidence of sameness) remain queryable as separate, unresolved records rather than being auto-merged

Any committed automatic merge records what evidence justified it, distinct from the coarse signal that merely surfaced the candidate, and records which mechanism/decision-path performed the merge (e.g. a rule-set or code-path identity), so that a false-merge class recurring across code changes is detectable

The pre-merge state (the original separate records, or enough information to reconstruct them) survives the merge, whether via retained source rows, an audit log, a correction/supersession record, or an equivalent mechanism — physical non-deletion is not required, but irrecoverable loss of the pre-merge identities is not acceptable
A human-reviewed or evidence-gated merge path exists for candidates that don't meet the automatic-merge bar, rather than such candidates being silently dropped or force-merged

evidence.summary: A coarse model_key fallback merged two genuinely different SKUs sharing a tier word; the identical bug class recurred independently months later in different code.
Un-deduplicated carrier/unlocked URLs sharing one regional partNumber produced 48 false new_product events, later reclassified and retained as evidence, not deleted.

Single-shared-entity clustering with no conservatism produced a merged-entity artifact that became the database's highest-scored 'story,' motivating a full architectural rebuild (proposal-layer + independence grouping) rather than a patch.

Conservative, evidence-gated, brand-by-brand allowlist policy: 'a brand only gets suffix-stripping rules once real evidence shows which suffixes are safe to collapse... until then its normalizer must be a conservative pass-through.' Zero confirmed false merges in the surveyed evidence.

notes: Pass 1 draft (docs/data-ontology/pass1/dossier-c3-identity-conservatism.md), from Pass 0B adjudication candidate C3 (docs/data-ontology/pass0/candidates/c3-identity-conservatism.md), from Pass 0A cluster entity-identity-coarse-key-merge (docs/data-ontology/pass0/clusters/entity-identity-coarse-key-merge.md). Deliberately does not choose among model number, source IDs, region+model, fingerprints, aliases, compound keys, or manual resolution as the identity mechanism — semiconductor-intelligence's gated proposal-layer and watch-clank's conservative allowlist are both conformant despite using entirely different mechanisms, which is the intended effect: this standard constrains the consequence of an identity decision (conservative default, evidence-gated commit, auditable, reversible), never the algorithm that produces it. Cross-Clank entity identity (the same real-world entity discovered by two different Clanks) is explicitly a separate, held concern (see Pass 0B adjudication candidate C7, HOLD/DEFER, blocked by clank-architecture's ADR-0002 DO_NOT_STANDARDISE position) and is out of scope for this standard, which binds within-Clank merges only. Version 2 (Pass 2.5, docs/data-ontology/pass2/review.md's STD-DATA-COM-003 section): REVISE verdict applied exactly, two tightenings only — FORBIDDEN 1's 'available' qualifier scoped to discriminators present in the records under consideration or the merged record (not world-knowledge, keeping the forbidden testable); acceptance 2 extended to require the merge audit record the mechanism/decision-path that performed the merge, directly motivated by oem-radar's false-merge class recurring across two different code paths. No universal confidence threshold, key hierarchy, or identity algorithm was added; no reach into cross-Clank identity; the conservative/evidence-gated/auditable/information-preserving core is unchanged. RATIFIED 2026-08-31 by operator ruling, Pass 3 ratification survey recommended RATIFY AS WRITTEN (posture framing evidence-faithful, no universal evidence bar offered as it would be algorithm prescription, no retirement offered as four independent incidents up to architectural-rebuild severity are the opposite of insufficient evidence), decision record decisions/0012-data-com-003-decision.md.
